record.original_question: Taking the above recurrences to represent the CG or steepest descent algorithm, determine conditions on $A$ that will insure that the norms of the vectors $r_k$ drop below the machine precision in finite precision arithmetic or show some examples where they do not.

evidence.quote: Taking the above recurrences to represent the CG or steepest descent algorithm, determine conditions on $A$ that will insure that the norms of the vectors $r_k$ drop below the machine precision in finite precision arithmetic or show some examples where they do not.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Consider the iterates produced by the conjugate gradient (CG) method or the steepest descent method applied to the linear system $Ax = b$, starting from some initial guess $x_0$ with initial residual $r_0 = b - A x_0$. In exact arithmetic these methods generate a sequence of approximate solutions $x_k$ and residual vectors $r_k = b - A x_k$ satisfying the standard recurrences:
- Steepest descent: $\alpha_k = \frac{r_k^T r_k}{r_k^T A r_k}$, $x_{k+1} = x_k + \alpha_k r_k$, $r_{k+1} = r_k - \alpha_k A r_k$.
- CG: with search directions $p_0 = r_0$, $\alpha_k = \frac{r_k^T r_k}{p_k^T A p_k}$, $x_{k+1} = x_k + \alpha_k p_k$, $r_{k+1} = r_k - \alpha_k A p_k$, $\beta_k = \frac{r_{k+1}^T r_{k+1}}{r_k^T r_k}$, $p_{k+1} = r_{k+1} + \beta_k p_k$.

Now suppose these recurrences are executed in finite-precision floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff $u$ (machine precision). The computed residual vectors $\tilde r_k$ may stagnate above $u\,\|b\|$ or below it depending on $A$.

Determine sufficient (and, where possible, necessary) conditions on the matrix $A$ (e.g., on its spectrum, condition number, eigenvalue distribution, or structure) under which the computed residual norms $\|\tilde r_k\|$ eventually fall below the machine precision level (e.g., $\|\tilde r_k\| \le c\, u\, \|b\|$ for a modest constant $c$) as $k$ grows. Alternatively, exhibit explicit examples of symmetric positive definite matrices $A$ for which $\|\tilde r_k\|$ never drops below the machine precision in either CG or steepest descent run in finite precision arithmetic.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this question was located. The behavior of finite-precision residuals in CG and steepest descent has been extensively studied (Greenbaum, Strakoš, Gutknecht, Paige, and others), and it is known that maximum attainable accuracy is governed by the gap between the true and updated residuals, but a complete characterization of matrices $A$ guaranteeing $\|\tilde r_k\|$ below machine precision is not established in the literature surveyed; the question appears to remain open in the general form posed.

status_evidence.title: Greenbaum: Estimating the attainable accuracy of recursively computed residual methods
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the gap between true and updated residuals in CG-type methods are derived, but no full characterization of when residuals reach machine precision is given.
status_evidence.claim: Existing analyses bound but do not fully characterize when residual norms drop below machine precision.
